bullets.title: Politician Cyrus Habib Leaves Office to Join the Jesuits
bullets.note: (_The New York Times_ — [@nytimes](https://twitter.com/nytimes)). Have you ever fantasized about walking off and leaving it all behind? This is the amazing story of one man, on track for ever-growing prestige and power, who did just that. Kudos to [Frank Bruni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Bruni) ([@FrankBruni](https://twitter.com/FrankBruni)) for a great piece. For more on Cyrus, here is [his Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrus_Habib).

bullets.section: Podcast I’m listening to once again —
bullets.title: Brilliant Minds of Trash and Sewage
bullets.note: Alec Baldwin ([@ABFalecbaldwin](https://twitter.com/ABFalecbaldwin)) — yes, that Alec Baldwin — is absolutely one of the best interviewers in the podcast game. Polymath [Matt Mullenweg](https://tim.blog/2015/02/09/matt-mullenweg/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf) recommended this short episode of [_Here’s the Thing_](https://www.wnycstudios.org/podcasts/heresthething) to me, and it doesn’t disappoint. Here’s a teaser: “New York City generates 1.3 billion gallons of wastewater every day. 16 million pounds of trash. Eight million pounds of recyclables. Think of the awesome engineering and effort behind making all of that ‘go away’ without our thinking about it.” Listen to this one for ten minutes. It will help you to see and appreciate the unseen that we so easily take for granted.

bullets.title: How we can face the future without fear, together
bullets.creator: Rabbi Lord Jonathan Sacks
bullets.note: . Rabbi Sacks was an incredible man, and he sadly passed away last Saturday. I’m sure he’s already helping those in need on the other side. To feel his brilliance and warmth of spirit, you might also enjoy [this conversation between Rabbi Sacks and David Brooks](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zfplRTXO5HA) or [my long-form podcast with him](https://tim.blog/2020/08/26/rabbi-lord-jonathan-sacks-2/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf), recorded just a few months ago. May he rest in peace, and my sincerest condolences to his family and loved ones.
